title: Assemble the four-pillar plan
intro: A financial plan isn't a list of products — it's a structure. Build it.
briefing: Route your income into a plan that survives a shock: protection before growth, a liquidity buffer so emergencies never touch long-term money, and every growth rupee aimed at a named goal.

rules.label: A liquidity buffer is funded directly
A monthly SIP runs from income
Every SIP is aimed at a named goal
Emergency money is never goal money
At least one goal has a name and a number

debrief: The structure you wired is the whole point: protection and liquidity hang directly off income — funded first, not from what's left over — while growth flows only through SIPs that point at NAMED goals. The one wire the inspector forbids is emergency → goal: the moment your buffer doubles as goal money, one hospital bill liquidates your long-term compounding at the worst possible time. Growth without protection and liquidity is a plan that only works when life cooperates.
